newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares ease 1.2 pct, more losses seen.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares ease 1.2 pct, more losses seen.

text.p: Slovenian shares fell 1.20 percent on Tuesday which traders attributed to uncertainty concerning the ratification of the association agreement with the European Union.

"I expect prices to continue falling until there is more fresh money on the market, which will happen only when foreign investors return, but if Slovenia does not ratify the association accord foreigners will stay away," one trader said.

The parliament is expected to take a vote on whether to ratify the agreement either on Wednesday or on its next session on May 20, but some Slovenians are pushing for a referendum on the issue, which could delay the vote.
The SBI index fell 15.87 points to 1,305.78. In two consecutive sessions the index fell by 4.1 percent.
Overall 15 shares fell and two rose, while 11 were untraded. Turnover rose to 106.8 million tolars from 79.5 million.
Traders said expectations of a return of foreign buyers to the market kept prices from tumbling even further.
In February the central bank blocked foreign portfolio investment, ordering foreign buyers to open share trading custody accounts at any of 14 licensed banks.
Since then the blue-chip index has dropped by more than 21 percent, while the average daily turnover shrunk to a third of its previous size.
Food maker Kolinska was the most actively traded share, down 3.29 percent to 1,910 tolars on volume of 12,855 shares on total turnover of 24.5 million tolars.
Slovenia's only port Luka Koper was the leading decliner, falling 4.68 percent to 1,792 tolars on volume of 2,965 shares on total turnover of 5.4 million tolars.
Traders said Luka's shares fell in technical reaction as they were over-priced in terms of business results and future outlook.
Brokerage Dadas was the top gainer, jumping 12.32 percent to 7,750 tolars on volume of 30 shares for a total volume of 231,700 tolars.

"I can not see any logical reason for such an increase and apart from that volume on that share was very low. Dadas is one of those shares whose movement are very difficult to predict," said Primoz Merhar, a trader at brokerage Proxy.

Trading volume of Dadas has been very small since March last year, when the Securities' Market Agency started procedures to ban Dadas' brokerage from trading, claiming it was rigging prices among its affiliated companies.
Since then the share has slumped by about 97 percent, while volume is down to a fraction of its previous daily average of over 1,000 shares per day.
